subject: clang++ 3.1 on Linux?  Mac is OK

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: clang++ 3.1 on Linux?  Mac is OK
parts:
Ben -- do the tests still fail for your clang++ 3.1
under Linux? If so, Daniel's probably the one to debug
the problem because it's in the validation code.

I upgraded to Xcode 4.4.1 when it was available and
and now I'm running clang++ 3.1 by default:

~/stan>clang++ --version
Apple clang version 3.1 (tags/Apple/clang-318.0.61) (based on LLVM 3.1svn)
Target: x86_64-apple-darwin11.4.2
Thread model: posix

The unit tests all pass, so everything looks OK.

I wonder how much we need to keep testing older
versions?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: clang++ 3.1 on Linux?  Mac is OK
parts:
On Wednesday, August 15, 2012 1:34:06 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Ben -- do the tests still fail for your clang++ 3.1
under Linux?  If so, Daniel's probably the one to debug
the problem because it's in the validation code.
Yes, attached is everything I have, which is scarcely more than what I posted before.

I wonder how much we need to keep testing older
versions?

For clang, I would say not to worry at all about older versions because approximately no one is "stuck" using an old version of clang. For g++, people may have no real choice but to use whatever version is installed on the server they use or whatever version is covered by the support contract they have. Not to mention CRAN.

Ben
